Name: Tomoe Gozen
Information:
**Tomoe Gozen**

A swordswoman raised by a secretive family in Cu Chullis, who raised their children with strict senses of duty toward their clan. They served as sentries for a greater noble family, being bred and trained as sentries, bodyguards, and vassals meant to never speak and only follow orders. Tomoe excelled even among the members of their elven family, finding themselves to be one of the greater archers in a dozen generations of elves in their country. Despite this, Tomoe’s tale is one of tragedy - of someone who came to possess a deep love, but was never to be loved in return, and found herself abandoned by all those around her.

**The Sky Folds**

Tomoe’s greatest legend was that of a conflict with an incarnation of Ivsil, the god of storms, who manifested to destroy the family she was charged to protect. Tomoe’s clan was almost entirely wiped out in the face of this war, but Tomoe held firm and stood against the sky god on horseback while their allies escaped. Through luck and intuition, as the god turned its attention from her to the escaping nobles, Tomoe chanced on a single dragon-slaying arrow she fired through the sky despite being blinded by her own blood in her eyes, and yet she struck a fatal blow across an impossible distance. This feat would be spoken of as Tomoe “folding the sky.” The remains of the god’s aspect would be merged with ancient heavenly wood to create a weapon for her as thanks for this event: the aptly named greatbow of lightning, Folding Sky.

**Downfall**

After saving her charges, Tomoe was adopted as the personal protector of the noble family her clan was sworn to save. The lord of these nobles, widowed during Ivsil’s attack, came to develop feelings for her - feelings she reciprocated. However, another surviving member of Tomoe’s clan - Tomoe’s brother - had grown jealous of her since her heroic acts to save the family, and orchestrated events to make it seem as though Tomoe had allowed the lord’s late wife to pass, unprotected during the attack. The lord would fight on her behalf, but Tomoe did not wish to besmirch his image, and so fled as though guilty and allowed these rumors to be believed. Still, she and the lord would meet privately once a month. Tomoe would be treated as a deserter, and concealed her identity to avoid the shame. Legends say she became a shrine maiden in Honokuni for a time, where she trained with a clan of female swordsmen.

**Sickness and Death**

Once, when she returned to see her lord, he did not show. She heard he had not made public appearances for some time, and feeling something wrong, she searched for answers about his fate, eventually escalating through rings of secrecy that led her to invade the stronghold she once protected. Storming it, she found her brother and demanded the truth. He supplied it: the lord had been exposed to a strange monster that emerged from a nearby hollow in the earth, and this sickness had begun to erode his memory. This disease was unlike anything known to modern medicine or magic.

Tomoe would flee, determined to search for answers, eventually ending up in the depths of an underground chamber in Retia’s country of Sermonway. Leads told her similar sickness had exuded from this place, and when she went to seek answers in these underground chambers she found a lake of mist and crystal, where the servants of several gods had erected barriers to prevent this mist (itself the source of the sickness) from escaping. Her presence awoke an ancient beast hiding there, a goliath born from the crystal, who she fought and defeated. She was not infected by the sickness, but was lethally wounded and unable to escape the tunnels. She collapsed in a hollow hundreds of feet below the earth, impossibly lit by moonlight, and died there, alone and unaided.

**Legacy**

Servants of a near-by temple of a night goddess would be dispatched by their sympathetic goddess, who found her body and constructed a shrine for her, marking a grave there, and would go on to spread her legend as they could find it. Tomoe’s spirit, unwilling to rest so long as the sickness that claimed her lover persisted, became a spirit bound to her shrine, waiting to guide any who came seeking the same perils she did and remind them not to live - or die - alone.

traits.name: Lightning Critical
traits.description: The spirit scores a critical hit on ranged weapon attack d20 results of 18, 19, or 20. When they score any critical hit they deal an additional 2d10 lightning damage, and the target must make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they are paralyzed until the start of the spirit’s next turn. On a success they are immune to being paralyzed this way until then.

traits.name: Saint Surge (Recharge 5-6)
traits.description: The spirit takes a second action on its turn.

traits.name: Unwavering Saint
traits.description: If the spirit is reduced to 0 hit points, the creature who defeated it must roll a d100. On a result equal to or less than twice the damage dealt to the saint that exceeded its hit points, it is successfully reduced to 0 hit points. Otherwise, it is reduced to 1 hit point instead.

traits.name: Wind Chain Mastery
traits.description: When the spirit makes a melee weapon attack, they may treat its reach as though it was 30 feet.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The spirit makes three weapon attacks.

actions.name: Spirit Naginata, +2
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (1d10 + 5) slashing damage plus 6 (1d10) lightning damage.

actions.name: Spirit Greatbow, +2
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (1d10 + 7) piercing damage plus 6 (1d10) lightning damage.

actions.name: Raikou Storm
actions.description: The spirit fires a lightning arrow at a point it can see within 150 feet, where it detonates in a 30-foot-radius sphere. Each creature in that sphere must make a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d10 lightning damage on a failure, or half as much damage on a success. Any creature who fails their saving throw by 5 points or more is stunned until the start of the spirit’s next turn.

bonus_actions.name: Majesty Stance
bonus_actions.description: Until the start of its next turn, all attacks made against the spirit have disadvantage. If one hits before then, this effect ends.

bonus_actions.name: Rising Flight
bonus_actions.description: Until the start of the spirit’s next turn, the spirit may walk on vertical and horizontal surfaces as though under the effects of the spider climb spell.

bonus_actions.name: Teleport
bonus_actions.description: The spirit shimmers out of existence and reappears in an unoccupied space within its remaining movement speed. The distance between these two spaces is subtracted from its remaining movement.

reactions.name: Counterfire
reactions.description: When a creature the spirit can see makes a ranged weapon attack while within range of its Spirit Greatbow, the spirit can make an attack using it against the attacker. If their attack roll is higher than the target’s, the attack misses automatically. This attack does not consider critical hits.
